about: Every namespace, call, and member a Decay script may name, derived from the host surface the analyzer and the runtime share, with a description of each and the names of each call's parameters. docs/scripting.md explains the design behind them.

globals.description: Creates automatically playing gameplay tweens owned by the calling script. Copies alias playback state. Advance occurs before the owner's subsequent updates using script delta. No automatic property binding. Curves: linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out. Finite endpoints and finite non-negative duration are required; zero duration completes immediately. Maximum 8192 retained handles per runner; dispose unused handles.
globals.name: Tween

globals.description: The interface drawn over the game: changing text and bars, and checking buttons and sliders.
globals.name: Ui

globals.description: The area of the screen the game is drawn in.
globals.name: Viewport

globals.description: The number without its minus sign: `abs(-3.0)` is `3`. Useful for distances and differences where only the size matters.
globals.name: abs

globals.description: The angle pointing from the origin towards the point (x, y), in radians. Use it to turn something to face a direction: `atan2(dy, dx)`.
globals.name: atan2

globals.description: Rounds up to a whole number: `ceil(2.1)` is `3`.
globals.name: ceil

globals.description: Keeps a number between a lowest and a highest value: `clamp(hp, 0.0, 100.0)` never goes below 0 or above 100.
globals.name: clamp

globals.description: The cosine of an angle in radians. With `sin`, turns an angle into a direction: `Vec2(cos(a), sin(a))`.
globals.name: cos

globals.description: The number e raised to a power. Mostly used for smooth movement that looks the same at any frame rate: `1.0 - exp(-speed * dt)`.
globals.name: exp

globals.description: Rounds down to a whole number: `floor(2.9)` is `2`.
globals.name: floor

globals.description: Blends between two numbers: `t` of 0 gives `a`, 1 gives `b`, and 0.5 gives halfway. Used for smooth movement and fades.
globals.name: lerp

globals.description: The larger of two numbers.
globals.name: max

globals.description: The smaller of two numbers.
globals.name: min

globals.description: Writes a message to the log, for checking what a script is doing. Accepts any value; combine text and values with `+`: `print("hp " + hp)`.
globals.name: print

globals.description: Rounds to the nearest whole number: `round(2.5)` is `3` and `round(-2.5)` is `-3`.
globals.name: round

globals.description: Whether a number is negative, zero or positive, as -1, 0 or 1. Handy for "which way is this moving?".
globals.name: sign

globals.description: The sine of an angle in radians. Good for bobbing and waving motion: `sin(Time.elapsed)`.
globals.name: sin

globals.description: The square root of a number.
globals.name: sqrt

types.description: The game's camera: moving the view and changing its engine-owned follow, confinement, and shake behavior.

members.description: Adds impact trauma to the authored behavior camera. Bigger amounts shake harder, up to 1, and the authored shake fades by itself.
members.name: add_trauma

members.description: Confines the authored behavior camera to the given world-space rectangle.
members.name: bounds

members.description: Removes runtime confinement from the authored behavior camera.
members.name: clear_bounds

members.description: Stops the authored behavior camera following a target.
members.name: clear_follow

members.description: Sets the follow dead-zone size for the authored behavior camera.
members.name: dead_zone

members.description: Makes the authored behavior camera follow an entity at runtime.
members.name: follow

members.description: Sets the world-space offset from the follow target used by the authored behavior camera.
members.name: follow_offset

members.description: Shakes the authored behavior camera at least this hard, up to 1: a smaller impact while a bigger one is still shaking changes nothing, so many small hits in a frame do not add up to the biggest shake.
members.name: impact

members.description: Sets the maximum follow speed of the authored behavior camera.
members.name: max_speed

members.description: How far the camera view is moved sideways from where it was placed in the scene.
members.name: pan_x

members.description: How far the camera view is moved up or down from where it was placed in the scene.
members.name: pan_y

members.description: How far the camera view is moved forwards or backwards from where it was placed in the scene.
members.name: pan_z

members.description: Changes the authored behavior camera's shake strength, frequency, and trauma decay.
members.name: shake

members.description: Sets how strongly the authored behavior camera smooths its follow movement.
members.name: smoothing

types.description: Creates automatically playing gameplay tweens owned by the calling script. Copies alias playback state. Advance occurs before the owner's subsequent updates using script delta. No automatic property binding. Curves: linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out. Finite endpoints and finite non-negative duration are required; zero duration completes immediately. Maximum 8192 retained handles per runner; dispose unused handles.

members.description: Stops at the current value; is_done is false. Restart can play it again.

members.name: is_done

members.name: is_paused

members.name: number

members.description: Reads the eased number, held at the exact target after completion.

members.name: pause

members.description: Linear elapsed fraction from 0 to 1; zero duration is 1.
members.name: progress

types.description: The interface drawn over the game: changing text and bars, and checking buttons and sliders.

members.description: Whether a button is being held down right now.
members.name: is_held

members.description: Whether the mouse or finger is over a button.
members.name: is_hovered

members.description: Whether a button was clicked this frame: pressed and let go while on it.
members.name: is_pressed

members.description: Shows part of an image, from 0 (none) to 1 (all). This is how health and progress bars work: `Ui.set_fill(bar, hp / max_hp)`.
members.name: set_fill

members.description: Puts a number into a text element. Its text is set up in the scene with a `{}` where the number goes, such as `"Score: {}"`.
members.name: set_number

members.description: Puts two numbers into a text element with two `{}` places, such as `"{}/{}"` for `45/100`.
members.name: set_numbers

members.description: Moves a slider to a value, kept within the slider's range.
members.name: set_slider_value

members.description: Changes the words a text element shows.
members.name: set_text

members.description: Whether the player moved a slider this frame.
members.name: slider_changed

members.description: The value a slider is set to.
members.name: slider_value

types.name: Ui

types.description: An image in the interface drawn over the game, such as a health bar or an icon, rather than in the game world.

members.description: Drawing order: higher numbers are drawn in front of lower ones.
members.name: layer

members.description: A colour the image is multiplied by. White leaves it unchanged; lowering `a` fades it out.
members.name: tint

types.name: UiImage

types.description: A managed Vec2 tween; read with Tween.vec2_value.
types.name: Vec2Tween

types.description: A managed Vec3 tween; read with Tween.vec3_value.
types.name: Vec3Tween

types.description: The area of the screen the game is drawn in.

members.description: The game view's width divided by its height: above 1 for a wide screen, below 1 for a phone held upright.
members.name: aspect

types.name: Viewport

types.description: Finding, creating and removing the objects in a game. Every object in a scene (a player, an enemy, a button) is an entity.

members.description: Removes an object, and everything attached to it, from the game. Used when an enemy dies or a bullet hits something.
members.name: despawn

members.description: Whether an object still exists. Check before using an object you stored earlier, since it may have been removed since.
members.name: exists

members.description: Finds an object by the name it was given in the scene, such as `World.find("Player")`. Gives `null` if there is none.
members.name: find

members.description: Whether an object has a tag, a label such as `"enemy"` given to it in the scene.
members.name: has_tag

members.description: Whether an object is switched on. An object switched off, or inside one that is, is hidden and does nothing.
members.name: is_active

members.description: The closest active object with an authored tag to a world-space Vec3 position, including parent transforms. Gives null if none has a usable transform. Equal distances keep world order.
members.name: nearest

members.description: Reads a number set up for another object's script, such as a bullet's damage, or gives `fallback` if there is none.
members.name: property_number

members.description: Sends a number to another object under a name, for its script to collect with `take_signal`. Older style: events and calling another script's functions are clearer.
members.name: send_signal

members.description: Switches an object, and everything inside it, on or off. This is how menus and screens are shown and hidden.
members.name: set_active

members.description: Attaches an object to another, so it moves, turns and scales with it. `null` detaches it.
members.name: set_parent

members.description: Sets a starting value on a newly created object's script, before it starts. For example, a bullet's speed right after spawning it.
members.name: set_property

members.description: Moves one corner, numbered 0 to 7, of this object's custom polygon shape.
members.name: set_shape_point

members.description: Creates a new object from a prefab, a reusable template such as a bullet or an enemy, and gives it back so you can position it.
members.name: spawn

members.description: Creates a new object from a prefab, already attached to a parent object.
members.name: spawn_child

members.description: Collects the numbers other scripts sent to this object under a name with `send_signal`, added together. Gives 0 when nothing arrived.
members.name: take_signal

members.description: Every switched-on object with a tag, as a list: `for enemy in World.with_tag("enemy") { ... }`. Looks through the whole game, so call it once per frame, not in a loop.
members.name: with_tag

members.description: A snapshot list of active tagged objects within an inclusive world-space radius of a Vec3 position, nearest first; ties keep world order. Skips unusable transforms. Empty when none match; over 8192 results is an error. Negative or NaN radii are errors; positive infinity searches the whole world.
members.name: within_radius

types.name: World
